title: Corrupt LanceDB fragments: table opens clean, count_rows lies, queries die
repro:
# ALL work on an APFS clone of the corpus; var/arxmcp/ never written.
S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-chris-dare-Personal-SourceCode/1295cdbb-487b-4884-af5b-60198b75dc76/scratchpad/data
cp -Rc /Users/chris.dare/Personal/SourceCode/arXMCP/var/arxmcp/index/lancedb-staging $S/ldb-a
cd /Users/chris.dare/Personal/SourceCode/arXMCP
# zero every data fragment in the clone, then open + query:
KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK=TRUE uv run python .claude/notes/chaos/2026-08-22/evidence/data/p5.py   # case C4/C5
observed:
[C4] zeroed 45 fragments
marker: CorpusVersionInfo(version=181, ... chunk_count=105)
open OK v= 181
count_rows: 4279
search5 EXC: RuntimeError lance error: Invalid user input: file does not appear to be a Lance file (invalid magic: [76, 65, 78, 67]), .../lance-file-4.0.0/src/reader.rs:471:24
to_arrow_rows EXC: RuntimeError lance error: Invalid user input: ...
[C5] truncated all fragments to 40%
open OK v= 181 / count_rows: 4279 / search5 EXC: RuntimeError lance error: LanceError(IO): Generic LocalFileSystem error: failed to fill whole buffer
AND (from p6.py) 'FALLBACK on C4 zeroed fragments' -> open_chunks_table_with_fallback returned DegradedState=None (i.e. HEALTHY) with rows: 4279, then the first search raised.
expected: server/resources.py:592-650 reconciles marker chunk_count against chunks_table.count_rows() at startup and flips /readyz to degraded. count_rows() reads Lance FRAGMENT METADATA only, so it returns the full 4279 even when every byte of every fragment is zeroed or truncated. open_chunks_table_with_fallback (server/corpus.py:175) therefore never sees a failure, returns DegradedState=None, and the server boots and reports READY on a corpus that cannot answer a single query. There is no read-side integrity probe (not even a 1-row scan) at startup. A one-row `.limit(1).to_list()` smoke read would catch every case here.

title: Shipped lancedb-staging marker says 105 chunks; table actually holds 4279
repro:

cat var/arxmcp/index/lancedb-staging/corpus-version.json
KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK=TRUE uv run python .claude/notes/chaos/2026-08-22/evidence/data/p1.py  # opens the CLONE, same bytes
expected: The bulk-ingest 'last paper wins' marker bug (known from prior sessions) means the on-disk marker under-reports by ~40x (105 vs 4279) and paper_count=1 vs the many distinct paper_ids actually present. With corpus_chunk_count_tolerance=0.05 (server/config.py:377) this corpus is PERMANENTLY degraded at every boot: compute_chunk_count_divergence fires, /readyz reports degraded(reason=chunk_count_diverged) forever. The degrade signal is therefore desensitised — an operator learns to ignore it, so a REAL divergence is invisible. Marker must be written as an aggregate, not per-paper.

title: no-repro: path hostility on identifiers — no reachable paper_id path collision
repro:
cd /Users/chris.dare/Personal/SourceCode/arXMCP
grep -rn 'replace("/"' server tools ingest
sed -n '58,72p' ingest/identifiers.py   # _PAPER_ID_FULL_PATTERN
sed -n '50,80p' tools/_notebook_common.py  # SLUG_RE + validate_slug
expected: Collision would need two distinct VALID ids mapping to one flat form. Impossible here: the old-style branch flattens to <archive>_<7 digits>, and the textbook branch to textbook_<slug> where the slug must START WITH A LETTER, so textbook/0001234 and textbook:<slug> can never meet; no accepted shape contains '_' natively, so no id can pre-image another's flat form. Slugs with /, .., :, NUL, unicode, emoji, 300 chars, leading '-', or '' are all rejected by SLUG_RE before any path construction. ONE inconsistency worth noting, not a collision: server/routes/ui.py:166 omits the ':' substitution the other three sites apply, so a textbook: id resolves to ar5iv/textbook:foo.html there vs parsed/textbook_foo/ elsewhere.

observed: Not run. Attack classes 3 (BM25/dense skew), 4 (two servers / concurrent writers / double notebook_ingest), 6 (hdiutil sparse-image disk pressure), 8 (HF_HUB_OFFLINE, truncated model cache, read-only model dir, KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK unset), and 9 (backdated/future/identical mtimes for corpus_freshness) produced no findings because they were not executed.

Classes 3, 4, 8 and 9 all require either a full server boot (model load dominates) or a write path into a notebook tree. The BM25 index root under var/arxmcp/index/bm25 (18M) is cloneable and class 3 is the highest-value of the untested set — recommend it first next run. Class 6 (hdiutil) is safe to run on a scratch image and was simply not reached. No test was skipped for safety reasons other than those recorded in CHAOS-DATA-13.
